**Playbook for the picket game**

**Hiding:** When a boat that fires on me next round exists, hide unpredictably and never repeat my previous cell — I hid at 5 in round 1 and again at 5 in round 6, and repeated cells are exactly what a rotating shooter catches. Track every note and public claim for hints about where others hide; with no read, spread across the line, not just the middle. Being fired at all six rounds and missed was luck, not skill — keep it that way by randomizing properly.

**Firing:** Never fire at the same cell round after round. Rotate systematically against my target — sweep the line or go center-out — so a stationary target eventually gets caught. I fired 5, 4, 5 at Foxtrot across rounds and never connected; a full sweep would have covered more ground. That said, treat firing as secondary income: 4 points a hit versus 5 a round from a mutual escort means the coalition is the real business. Never fire on Harbor — the 3-point jettison is nothing against being removed from play and losing all future escort earnings.

**Claims:** Always claim the true result. The office verifies anyway, honesty costs nothing, and credibility is what makes my escort proposals believable in notes.

**Notes:** Use notes to build the escort deal from round one, by name, to one specific boat — not an open offer to "any boat that names me." A named offer ("Echo to Gamma: I escort you every round if you escort me — confirm in your note") got confirmed and paid off every round. Once the pact is running, keep notes short and steady ("steady on station") — no need to renegotiate what's already locked in, and steady notes don't leak anything.

**Escort claims:** Once a mutual deal is confirmed, honor it every single round — including the final round. I claimed "none" in round 6 and threw away 5 points for absolutely no reason; there is no tomorrow to defect toward in a finitely repeated game, but also no gain from abandoning the pair on the last hand. The only reason to break a pact is if my partner defected first.

**General:** Score the game before playing it. A confirmed mutual escort pays 5/round — 25+ over a six-round patrol — which dwarfed everything else: my 19 came almost entirely from the Gamma pact, while six rounds of shooting earned zero. Spend round 1 on the note-stage coalition-building, keep the pact warm every round after, and treat the firing order as noise. Final standings came from whoever collected steady points, not whoever fired cleverly.

1.text:
**Playbook**

When asked to hide, I pick a cell and vary it round to round; I never settle into a predictable cell, because the boat shooting at me reads my pattern. In this episode my randomized hiding kept me unhit through all six rounds while my shots all missed, which suggests random hiding works and random firing does not — my opponents may be hiding predictably if I could read them. So: hide uniformly at random, but when firing, try to exploit any pattern in the target's past behavior (notes, past hits against them, common cells) rather than pure random.

When posting my station note, keep it uninformative about position and plans. My attempt to use notes for escort coordination ("Foxtrot will escort Echo this round; Echo, name me back") produced no reciprocation across six rounds — Echo and Gamma both kept posting "steady on station" and never named me. So do not count on note-based coordination changing anyone's behavior; treat notes as cheap talk at best.

When firing, follow the standing order target — deviating gains nothing, and Harbor's threat makes firing on Harbor strictly bad despite the 3-point payroll. Never fire on Harbor. For the fire cell: pure randomization went 0-for-6. Next time, vary cells but bias toward cells the target has been hit in or plausibly reuses; also consider firing at the same cell as my own hide cell is irrelevant — pick independently of my hide.

When claiming my shot result, always report truthfully — the claim is forced to match the office's private result. No decision here; echo it immediately.

At the escort stage: the mutual escort payout (5 points each) is real and worth chasing, but only mutual naming pays — a one-sided name earns nothing, and I earned nothing all game by naming boats who never named me back. Rules of thumb:
- Only name a boat that has actually named me in a previous round's escort stage, or that has posted an explicit commitment naming me.
- Never name a boat not in the game (I once wrote "Bravo" — no such station — a wasted move). Validate the name against the actual roster.
- If no boat has shown any reciprocation tendency after the first couple of rounds, naming is free but the expected value is low; keep naming the most plausible counterpart anyway since "none" is guaranteed zero, but do not structure my play around the payout.

Priority order, revised: hits (4 each, the actual differentiator — I scored -1 solely from being hit costs... in fact I was never hit; my -1 came from nothing) > mutual escort (5, but only if reciprocated — treat as opportunistic, not a plan) > avoiding being hit (-1 each, handled by random hiding). The real lesson: I lost because I never landed a hit. Put more effort into fire-cell prediction and less into coordination schemes that depend on silent opponents responding to cheap talk.

General habits: keep replies to exactly the bracketed tokens requested; keep reasoning to one short line; never improvise names or targets outside the validated set.

2.text:
PLAYBOOK

**Hiding:** Never pick mid-line cells like 5; boats that fire randomly hit the middle most. When I am the ordered target of the round's shooter, hide at an extreme cell (1, 2, 8, or 9), rotating unpredictably and avoiding any cell I've used before. In the episode I played, hiding at extremes kept me unhit all six rounds — this line worked, keep it.

**Firing:** Fire at my ordered target every round (the office validates targets and the standing order seems enforced anyway — never try to fire at Harbor). Don't default to cell 5; rotate across extremes and unused cells. Expect misses: with a 1-in-9 search, all my shots missed all round and that was fine — the escort income carried my score. Don't burn note-space or mental effort trying to engineer hits; treat shooting as a small lottery, not a strategy.

**Claims:** The office forces my claim to match the private result — report truthfully and don't agonize.

**Escort claims — confirmed as the core income.** Proposing a mutual escort deal through my note and then claiming my partner every round worked: the escort payments were my entire positive score. Protocol that worked: (1) at the note stage of round 1, propose "Gamma escorts Echo if Echo escorts Gamma — mutual +5 every round"; (2) at every escort stage, claim the proposed partner regardless of whether they've confirmed yet — claiming costs nothing if unreciprocated; (3) if my first-choice partner never reciprocates but the other boat does, switch to the reciprocator; (4) stick with a confirmed partner all rounds. Re-propose the deal in a note if it seems to lapse.

**Partner choice:** Prefer the boat that is NOT my firing target and is NOT firing at me, if such a one exists — the ordered target relationship and escort partnership can coexist (I fired at Echo and still escorted with Echo), but a boat taking hits from me may defect. In practice the deal held anyway, so don't overthink it.

**Notes:** Use notes every round for coordination — the escort proposal, hide-pattern conventions ("evens then odds so we don't hit each other"), and gentle reminders to keep claiming me. Other boats mostly post filler ("steady on station"), so an explicit proposal stands out and can be accepted silently via their escort claim. Keep the note short and actionable.

**Scoring math:** a hit is +4 to me, a hit on me is only -1, and a mutual escort is +5 each per round — up to +30 over six rounds, dwarfing everything else. Escort deals dominate: secure the partnership first, treat shooting as secondary, take hits on the chin rather than breaking cooperation to dodge.

**Endgame:** Watch the points table at the hide stage. If I'm within reach of the leader only via escort payments, prioritize keeping the deal alive in the final round — propose it again in the note and claim the partner one last time. A last-round defection gains nothing (unreciprocated claims cost zero), so there is no reason ever to claim "none" once a candidate partner exists.
